excerpts.author: andi9314
excerpts.content: I disagree. If we assume that the average user was someone who used to wait 1 min for his transaction to go through pre-1559, he will also be waiting roughly the same amount of time under 1559. We are not changing the average block size, so it can't be that everyone can now be included in the next block after 1559, unless 1559 reduces transaction demand. The average user will often find the base fee too high for him. He will just submit with lower base fee and wait for the base fee to go down, just as he submits with the "average" gas price pre-1559 and waits for his tx to go through.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If the user is willing to pay significantly over the base fee then they will be included next block in most cases.  At the very least, they'll be included next block in at least 50% of cases.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: The big difference here is that a user can bid their willingness to pay and then pay the least amount possible for rapid inclusion.  This is quite different from having to try to bid *barely enough so you don't overpay*.

excerpts.author: andi9314
excerpts.content: 2x full block would happen whenever gas price is rapidly rising or jumping. Which is as expected, but I suspect it could happen even when gas isn't on a clear upward trend, because when the current block is expected to go above the target size, everyone knows the next block will have a higher fee, so they will try to get included in the current, cheaper block.
